subject: explanation of sampler parameters in rstan, shinystan (minor)

messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: explanation of sampler parameters in rstan, shinystan (minor)
parts:
Hello,

when trying to change the target acceptance probability/statistic/rate in rstan I first had to look up that the name of the acceptance rate parameter "delta" in the cmdstan manual.
Maybe it is possible to add a brief description of sampler parameters with non-selfexplanatory names also to rstan?
E.g. 
...
2. adapt_gamma, the regularization scale during adaptation (double, positive, defaults to 0.05)
3. adapt_delta, the target acceptance statistic during adaptation (double, between 0 and 1, defaults to 0.8)
4. adapt_kappa, the relaxation exponent during adaptation (double, positive, defaults to 0.75) 
...

In the same vein one could give the name of the control parameter in shiny stan.
E.g: 
...  By setting the target acceptance parameter to a value closer to [e.g. with rstan stan(...,control = list(adapt_delta = .9))] ....


Alternatively one could add a warning like "Read sections 7.4 in the cmdstan manual and  section 54 of the stan reference before changing sampler parameters ..." to the rstan manual and shinystan ... :-)




I also found that the default delta is said to be .8 on page 40 of the cmdstan manual but .65 on page 54 of the same manual. 
It probably should also be .8 on page 54.

Guido

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: explanation of sampler parameters in rstan, shinystan (minor)
parts:
Right. It just says

• adapt_engaged (logical)

• adapt_gamma (double, positive, defaults to 0.05)

• adapt_delta (double, between 0 and 1, defaults to 0.8)

• adapt_kappa (double, positive, defaults to 0.75)

• adapt_t0 (double, positive, defaults to 10)

• adapt_init_buffer (integer, positive, defaults to 75)

• adapt_term_buffer (integer, positive, defaults to 50)

• adapt_window (integer, positive, defaults to 25)

without any explanation. I think it'd help to add descriptions. They're
all in the Stan manual. So at least we should point to that. There's the
issue of not wanting to duplicate doc, because it's so easy to get doc
out of synch.

- Bob
